items.title: Outbound request guard (SSRF) and screenshot pixel limit
items.body:
## Summary

Two hardening changes a penetration test would report.

### Outbound requests (SSRF)

Notification webhooks, CI provider APIs and OIDC (discovery, token, userinfo, JWKS) now go through `outboundFetch` (`apps/api/src/common/outbound.ts`):

- an undici `Agent` whose connector checks **every address the host resolves to, at connection time** — also for redirects and IP literals (which skip DNS). Connections aren't reused, so each request is resolved and checked anew (DNS rebinding);
- **always refused:** loopback, link-local (incl. `169.254.169.254`), other cloud metadata addresses (`fd00:ec2::254`, `100.100.100.200`, `192.0.0.192`), unspecified, multicast, reserved; IPv4-mapped and NAT64 forms count as IPv4;
- **private networks** (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, 100.64/10, fc00::/7) **allowed by default**, `OUTBOUND_ALLOW_PRIVATE=false` refuses them — on-prem GitLab/Bitbucket/IdPs are common in self-hosted installs; trade-off documented in `docs/security/settings.md`;
- `OUTBOUND_ALLOWED_HOSTS`: host names, `*.domain`, addresses, CIDR ranges — exceptions to all rules; validated at startup;
- settings (webhook target, `ciApiUrl`, OIDC issuer) reject refused IP literals and `localhost` with a 400 on save;
- failed calls report status or network error only: webhook and CI response bodies are no longer logged, OIDC errors no longer echo JSON parse errors (which contain the body) or a non-URL `issuer` field.
- JWKS: `createRemoteJWKSet` (Node `http`, outside the guard) is replaced by guarded fetch + `createLocalJWKSet`, cached 10 min, refetched for unknown key IDs (≤ every 30 s).
- SAML needs nothing: the entry point is only a browser redirect.

### Screenshot pixel limit

`MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` (default 50 MP — a 1280 px wide page at DPR 2 up to Chromium's 16,384 px capture height is 42 MP) is checked from the PNG IHDR **before decoding**, for the image, the baseline and the padded comparison canvas. Too large → 400 `Snapshot "X": The image is 100000×100000 pixels (10000 megapixels); at most 50 megapixels are allowed (MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS)`. The check runs on the main thread (error class survives) and again in the worker. `@optik/core` exports `pngSize`, `checkPngPixels`, `ImageTooLargeError`, `DEFAULT_MAX_PIXELS`; `computeDiff`/`diffImages` take `maxPixels`.

### Docs

New page `docs/security/settings.md` (in the sidebar) with the address table, the private-network default and its trade-off, and the pixel limit; the variables in `docs/install/configuration.md`; *Built in* in `docs/security/index.md`; the known issues in the whitepaper and pen test scope now describe the remaining trade-off; `docs/privacy.md`, questionnaire. Changeset starts with `Security:` and has an `Upgrade:` note (integrations on `localhost` need `OUTBOUND_ALLOWED_HOSTS`). `vitepress build` passes (dead links checked).

## Test plan

- [x] `apps/api` unit tests (74), incl. `src/common/outbound.spec.ts`: address classes, allowlist, IP literal / DNS / redirect checks at connection time
- [x] `apps/api` e2e (232 passed, 2 skipped as before), new `test/outbound.e2e-spec.ts` (settings refusal, webhooks/CI/OIDC refused at connection time, no response bodies in answers) and `test/image-limits.e2e-spec.ts` (10-gigapixel PNG of < 100 bytes → 400, configured limit, comparison canvas)
- [x] `@optik/core` tests (18), new `test/image-size.test.mjs`
- [x] `tsc --noEmit`, `nest build`
- E2e env allows `127.0.0.1` (fake servers) via `OUTBOUND_ALLOWED_HOSTS` in `test/setup/env.ts`

items.title: feat(oss): support environment-owned ECS RAM role authentication
items.body:
## Description

When WeKnora runs on Alibaba Cloud ECS with an attached RAM role, its environment-configured OSS storage requires a permanent AK/SK pair. This adds explicit `ecs_ram_role` authentication to that server-owned storage, using temporary credentials with automatic caching/refresh and SecurityToken signing. Existing configurations still default to `access_key`.

**Identity boundary:** ECS RAM role authentication is restricted to deployment environment configuration and its read-only `Source=env` storage backend snapshots. Tenant-controlled Create, Update, TestRaw, legacy tenant storage configuration and storage-engine checks reject role authentication before contacting metadata or OSS. The server owns `Source`; tenants cannot promote a backend to environment ownership. Persisted tenant role configurations are also rejected during runtime resolution, including disabled rows, and policy denials cannot fall back to the global storage identity in file proxies, knowledge operations, image uploads, analysis or storage URL resolution. No tenant opt-in switch is provided.

- Add `OSS_AUTH_TYPE` / `OSS_ROLE_NAME` and persisted authentication fields for environment-owned OSS backends. Temporary credentials are never saved in configuration.
- Share the SDK credentials provider between main and temporary bucket clients while copying the configuration before changing the temporary region.
- Bound each ECS metadata request to a 1-second timeout and one attempt. Failed lookups are not cached. Log only safe error categories/status codes and return a fixed actionable message without metadata response bodies or credentials.

items.title: bug(skill): metadata sizing example never matches the xlarge case

labels.name: status:withdrawn
labels.description: Withdrawn by the contributor during submission triage; retained for reference.

items.body:
## Description

`src/os-skills/aliyun/aliyun-ecs/references/metadata-api.md` lines ~113-116 ("根据实例规格动态配置") size a worker pool from the instance type:

```bash
INSTANCE_TYPE=$(curl -s http://100.100.100.200/latest/meta-data/instance-type)
case $INSTANCE_TYPE in
  *large*) WORKERS=4 ;;
  *xlarge*) WORKERS=8 ;;
esac
```

`case` takes the first matching pattern, and `*large*` is listed before `*xlarge*`. Every xlarge instance type also contains the substring `large` (e.g. `ecs.g7.xlarge`, `ecs.c6.2xlarge`), so the `*xlarge*) WORKERS=8` branch is dead code for all real inputs: users following the example provision 4 workers on xlarge-sized machines and never get the intended 8. Reproduction (extracted verbatim from the doc, run with xlarge inputs):

```console
$ for t in ecs.g7.xlarge ecs.c6.2xlarge ecs.g7.large; do
    WORKERS=0; INSTANCE_TYPE=$t
    case $INSTANCE_TYPE in *large*) WORKERS=4 ;; *xlarge*) WORKERS=8 ;; esac
    echo "$t -> WORKERS=$WORKERS"
  done
ecs.g7.xlarge -> WORKERS=4
ecs.c6.2xlarge -> WORKERS=4     # should be 8
ecs.g7.large -> WORKERS=4
```

## Suggested fix

Reorder the patterns so the more specific `*xlarge*` arm is matched first (`*xlarge*) WORKERS=8 ;; *large*) WORKERS=4 ;;`). With the reorder, the same loop prints `8 / 8 / 4` as intended.

items.title: feat(security): SAFE_URL_ALLOWED_HOSTS operator allowlist for private-network URLs
items.body:
## Problem

The SSRF guard (`docsgpt/security/safe_url.py`) rejects any user-supplied URL whose host resolves to a loopback, private, link-local, multicast, reserved or CGNAT address, with no override. On intranet-only deployments this breaks:

- **PAT → "create tool"** (`POST /api/user/tokens/<id>/tool`) always returns 400, because the instance's own URL resolves to a private IP.
- API tools, MCP tools, `read_webpage`, monitors and custom model base URLs can't reach internal services, which is the main use case on such installs.

## Change

New list setting **`SAFE_URL_ALLOWED_HOSTS`** (comma or JSON list, same `EnvList` pattern as `WEBPUSH_EXTRA_ALLOWED_HOSTS`). The default is empty, so nothing changes unless an operator sets it.

- **Hostname entry**: an exact, case-insensitive match in IDNA form. A URL with that host passes the private-address check for whatever it resolves to. `evil.example.com` does not match `example.com`.
- **IP / CIDR entry** (`10.16.0.0/16`): any resolved address inside it passes.
- **Never allowed**, whatever is listed: link-local (`169.254.0.0/16`, `fe80::/10`), the cloud metadata endpoints `fd00:ec2::254`, `100.100.100.200` and `metadata.google.internal`, and unspecified addresses. IPv4-mapped IPv6 is judged as IPv4.
- **Loopback** passes only through an explicit IP/CIDR entry (`127.0.0.1`, `::1`), never through a hostname such as `localhost` or a listed name that resolves to loopback.

Enforcement lives in `allowed_by_operator()` in `safe_url.py` and is used in two places:

- `_validate_and_pick_ip`, so `validate_user_base_url`, `pinned_request`, `pinned_fetch_bytes`, `pinned_post`, `pinned_httpx_client` and `guarded_async_client` all inherit it. DNS pinning is unchanged: the validated IP is the one dialed, and every resolved address must be public or allowed.
- `core/url_validation.validate_url`, the older create-time check used by MCP/API tool save, agent import, S3 custom endpoints and the website loaders. Without this, MCP tools on internal hosts would still be refused at save time even though dispatch allowed them.

The PAT tool refusal now tells the operator about `SAFE_URL_ALLOWED_HOSTS`.

## Docs

- Settings reference regenerated.
- New "Allowing private hosts" section in `Deploying/Security`.
- Removed the "there is no allowlist" statements from the API Tool, MCP Tools, Connectors and custom-tool pages.

## Tests

- Empty allowlist: private hosts stay blocked; all existing tests are unchanged and pass.
- An allowlisted hostname resolving to 10.x passes `validate_user_base_url`, and `pinned_request` dials the pinned IP with the original `Host`. The same holds for `guarded_async_client`.
- CIDR: an address inside passes, an address outside is blocked, and a mixed resolution (allowed + not allowed) is blocked.
- Metadata and link-local addresses, `0.0.0.0`/`::` and `metadata.google.internal` stay blocked even when listed. A `localhost` entry doesn't unlock loopback, and a hostname entry resolving to 127.0.0.1 is still refused.
- Hostname match is exact and IDNA-aware.
- `validate_url` honors the same rules.
- The PAT tool route returns 400 before the host is listed and 201 after; the 400 message names the setting.

`ruff check` is clean. `tests/security`, `tests/core`, `tests/agents`, `tests/api`, `tests/parser/remote`, `tests/monitors`, `tests/llm` and `tests/notifications` pass. `test_default_model_routing::test_is_quiet_for_a_working_setup` also fails on `main` because of a local model YAML on the test machine.

## Deployment notes

- New optional env var; there are no migrations or dependency changes.
- Every user of an instance can point tools at a listed host, so operators should list only the services users should reach. The Security docs say so.

  * Operators can configure `SAFE_URL_ALLOWED_HOSTS` with exact hostnames or IP/CIDR entries to allow selected private-network destinations for outbound URL access, including API Tool and MCP connections.

items.body: # why Closes #3002. A context with no configured domain policy fails open. `getDomainPolicyDecision` returns `continue` for every URL when the policy is `null`, and the extension never enables `Fetch` interception, so an agent-driven session can reach cloud metadata endpoints and link-local services on the browser machine. The gap matters most in unattended runs, where nobody reads the `debug` log that records a block. # what changed - The baseline is now the default value of the policy: `getEffectiveDomainPolicy(configured)` returns `configured ?? BASELINE_DOMAIN_POLICY` in `packages/extension/understudy/domainPolicy.ts`. `getDomainPolicy()` still reports the caller's policy, `null` while none is set. - `BASELINE_BLOCKED_RULES` covers `169.254.*`, `[fe80:*]`, `[::ffff:*]`, `[fd00:ec2::254]`, `100.100.100.200`, `metadata.google.internal`, and `metadata.goog`. The existing `toBlocklistFetchPatterns` compiles them into precise per-host patterns, so unrelated requests are never paused, and loopback, RFC1918, and ordinary browsing are untouched. - A new `glob` rule variant carries the range prefixes. User patterns cannot produce one: `normalizeDomainPattern` returns `Exclude`. - `BrowserContext` resolves the effective policy at every enforcement site, and the `Fetch.disable` branch is deleted because the effective policy is never null. `setDomainPolicy(null)`, `{}`, and empty arrays return the context to the default posture. - A baseline block logs one `warn` per context, since the per-block log stays at `debug`. - When `Fetch.enable` fails at attach and the caller configured no policy, the target keeps running and the failure is logged as an error. Callers who configured a policy keep the existing fail-closed target close. - `packages/docs/v4/reference/context.mdx` states the default posture in all three language tabs, and `packages/docs/v4/integrations/overview.mdx` names it in the security boundary. `packages/docs/v3` is untouched because that lineage does not ship this extension. ## Tradeoffs - An explicit policy replaces the baseline instead of merging with it. Union semantics would add a second precedence tier, and a carve-out still could not name an IPv6 literal. The cost is that a blocklist-only policy drops the metadata rules, so `setDomainPolicy` logs the replacement at `info` and the reference page says so. - IPv4-mapped spellings are blocked as a class through the `[::ffff:*]` prefix, because Chrome canonicalizes them to a hex form (`[::ffff:a9fe:a9fe]`) that no IPv4 rule matches. Mapped loopback is blocked with them. - Reaching an IPv6 baseline host requires replacing the baseline, because domain patterns cannot express a bracketed literal. Relaxing validation is a follow-up. - The IPv6 rule matches the `fe80:` prefix, which covers the canonical link-local spellings. The rest of `fe80::/10` would need four more glob rules for spellings nobody writes. - WebSocket and service-worker traffic stays outside the policy, as it already does when a policy is configured. That gap is #2945. ## Blast radius Every page and iframe session now enables `Fetch` with the baseline patterns, so `Fetch.enable` runs on the attach path even when no policy is configured. A rejected pattern or a flaky enable would previously close the target; with no caller policy it now logs and continues, which keeps the fail-closed guarantee for callers who asked for enforcement without letting a default break a page. The browse CLI and the Python and Go SDKs inherit the posture through the extension they bundle. # test plan - `pnpm exec vitest run packages/extension/understudy/domainPolicy.test.ts packages/extension/tests/understudy-context-baseline-policy.test.ts` (32 tests) covers the baseline decision set through the real URL parser, the exact pattern list, the once-per-context warning, and both attach-time failure paths. - `pnpm exec vitest run packages/extension/tests packages/extension/understudy` (449 tests) is green. - `CHROME_PATH=… pnpm run test:integration -- packages/sdk-ts/tests/integration/contextDomainPolicy.test.ts` runs 11 cases in real Chrome: 6 pre-existing and 5 new. Against the extension built from `main`, the three default-posture cases fail and the same three pass with this change. - `just check` and `just test` pass. Both were run with turbo concurrency 1, because parallel typecheck and lint exceed this machine's memory. - `packages/sdk-go/internal/extensionassets/stagehand-extension.zip` is regenerated, so `extensionpack --check` passes. --- ## Summary by cubic A context with no domain policy now blocks cloud metadata and link-local hosts by default, instead of failing open. `getEffectiveDomainPolicy` falls back to a baseline blocklist when no policy is set, so agent-driven sessions can no longer reach those hosts silently. **Behavior** - The baseline covers `169.254.*`, `[fe80:*]`, `[::ffff:*]`, `[fd00:ec2::254]`, `100.100.100.200`, `metadata.google.internal`, and `metadata.goog`. - Setting a policy replaces the baseline; clearing with `null` or an empty object returns to the default posture. - `Fetch.enable` now runs on every attach. When it fails with no policy configured, the target logs an error and keeps running; the fail-closed target close still applies when a policy is set. - A baseline block logs one `warn` per context, while per-block logs stay at `debug`. - v4 docs state the default posture in the TypeScript, Python, and Go tabs. **Tradeoffs** - An explicit policy replaces rather than merges with the baseline, so a blocklist-only policy drops the metadata rules. - `[::ffff:*]` blocks all IPv4-mapped IPv6 spellings because Chrome canonicalizes them to hex; mapped loopback is blocked with them. - An IPv6 baseline host is only reachable by replacing the baseline with an explicit policy, since domain patterns cannot express a bracketed literal. Written for commit 80c4c2a5b6b105d8e0dcec60919dea3d433e5d73. Summary will update on new commits.

items.title: fix: prevent SSRF via DNS rebinding with comprehensive IP validation (#1530)
items.body:
## Description

The webhook URL validation in _validate_webhook_url had several weaknesses that made SSRF via DNS rebinding possible:

1. **No DNS resolution** — The function only checked the hostname string itself (e.g., literal IP, .internal/.local suffix), but never actually resolved the hostname to IP addresses. An attacker could configure a hostname that initially resolves to a public IP (passing validation) but then switches to an internal IP after the TTL (DNS rebinding).

2. **Incomplete IP blocklist** — The cloud metadata IP check was hardcoded to only 169.254.169.254, missing other known metadata IPs (100.100.100.200 for Alibaba Cloud, 192.0.0.192 for AWS).

3. **Weak internal hostname detection** — Only .internal and .local suffixes were blocked, missing patterns like .lan, .intranet, .private, .corp.

## Changes

- Added import socket for DNS resolution
- Defined comprehensive blocklists: BLOCKED_IP_NETWORKS (all RFC1918 and special-use ranges), CLOUD_METADATA_IPS (3 known metadata endpoints), INTERNAL_HOSTNAME_SUFFIXES (6 suffixes), INTERNAL_HOSTNAME_EXACT (6 names)
- Added _is_ip_blocked() helper that checks private/loopback/link-local/reserved/multicast flags, network membership, and cloud metadata IPs
- Rewrote _validate_webhook_url: resolves **all** IP addresses via socket.getaddrinfo(), validates every resolved IP against the blocklist, and adds hostname suffix/pattern matching

## Related Issue

Closes #1530

items.title: feat: Packer + host bootstrap split for Alicloud (phase 5)
items.body:
## Context

#83 lays the Lambda-side groundwork for multi-cloud blitzlog.
#84 lands the Alicloud `SecretStore` + `ObjectStore` bodies.
The follow-up Phase 3 issue lands the Alicloud `ComputeProvider`.
Phase 4 splits the Terraform. This issue is **Phase 5**: the
Packer pipeline + host bootstrap that runs *on* the EC2/ECS
instance.

The Packer-baked host image today
(`infra/packer/agent-docker-ubuntu.pkr.hcl` and
`infra/packer/scripts-docker-ubuntu/`) is AWS-shaped:

- `01-system.sh` installs `awscli` + `docker-ce`.
- `02-systemd.sh` deploys `watchdog.sh` and the
  `blitzlog-agent.service` systemd unit.
- `03-bake-images.sh` `docker pull`s the agent image, tars it
  to `/opt/blitzlog/images/`, downloads the Whisper model via
  `aws s3 cp`.
- `watchdog.sh` does `aws s3 cp` for log/session uploads and
  `aws s3 rm` for bot-pool lock release; uses IMDSv2 at
  `169.254.169.254` to fetch region + instance-id.
- `lambda/scripts/{assisted,autonomous}.py` (rendered into the
  user-data heredoc) do `aws s3 cp` for session restore and
  `aws s3 cp` for the Whisper model download; read SSM via
  `aws ssm get-parameter`.

The Alicloud equivalent needs a parallel tree:

- `aliyun` CLI instead of `awscli`; `ossutil` for S3-shaped
  object storage.
- ECS + VPC + VSwitch instead of EC2 + VPC + Subnet.
- Aliyun metadata endpoint `100.100.100.200` instead of IMDSv2.
- RAM roles (instance RAM roles) instead of IAM instance
  profiles; KMS / Parameter Store instead of SSM Parameter Store.
- The container image (`packages/images/agent/Dockerfile`) is
  *unchanged* — it already runs on any Ubuntu 24.04+ host with
  Docker.

## Goal

Introduce `infra/packer/agent-ecs-ubuntu.pkr.hcl` and
`infra/packer/scripts-ecs-ubuntu/` so `BLITZLOG_PROVIDER=alicloud`
picks a parallel AMI at Lambda launch time. Today the Lambda
hard-codes the Ubuntu Packer build via `/blitzlog/<env>/agent-ami-id-docker-ubuntu`;
Phase 4 introduced `BLITZLOG_PROVIDER` — Phase 5 makes the
host-bootstrap side match.

## New file tree

```
infra/packer/
  agent-docker-ubuntu.pkr.hcl   # existing — unchanged
  agent-ecs-ubuntu.pkr.hcl      # NEW
  scripts-docker-ubuntu/        # existing — unchanged in #83
    01-system.sh
    02-systemd.sh
    03-bake-images.sh
    05-publish-ami-id.sh
    watchdog.sh
  scripts-ecs-ubuntu/           # NEW
    01-system.sh                # installs aliyun CLI + ossutil + docker-ce
    02-systemd.sh               # mirrors the systemd unit, references the new watchdog
    03-bake-images.sh           # docker pull + ossutil cp for the model
    05-publish-ami-id.sh        # publishes to Aliyun Parameter Store under
                                #   /blitzlog/<env>/agent-ami-id-ecs-ubuntu
    watchdog.sh                 # same shape as the AWS watchdog but
                                #   - metadata endpoint 100.100.100.200
                                #   - ossutil cp instead of aws s3 cp
                                #   - Aliyun ECS DeleteInstances for terminate
```

## User-data heredoc rewrite (in this issue)

`lambda/scripts/{assisted,autonomous}.py` and
`lambda/scripts/_common.py::_read_secrets_from_ssm_script` today
hard-code `aws s3 cp` and `aws ssm get-parameter`. In Phase 5 they
become provider-dispatched:

- A new helper `lambda/scripts/_common.py::_read_secrets_dispatcher(issue_number, local_llm)`
  branches on `BLITZLOG_PROVIDER` and returns the appropriate heredoc
  body.
- The AWS branch is byte-identical to the pre-PR
  `_read_secrets_from_ssm_script` (the `if BLITZLOG_PROVIDER == "aws"`
  branch is the existing function body extracted verbatim).
- The Alicloud branch uses `ossutil` + the Aliyun metadata endpoint
  + Aliyun KMS or Parameter Store reads.

This is the first issue that touches `lambda/scripts/`. It is
explicitly the overlap with the watchdog-abstraction issue — the two
issues are independent in the bash library (host-only), but
overlap in the Python heredoc (the user-data). The Python heredoc
rewrite belongs here because the heredoc is rendered *for* a
specific AMI's tools (ossutil is only present on the Alicloud AMI,
so the heredoc must dispatch on `BLITZLOG_PROVIDER`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `infra/packer/agent-ecs-ubuntu.pkr.hcl` exists and is wired
      into the same release.yml pipeline as the AWS Packer build
      (a new matrix axis `provider = ["aws", "alicloud"]`).
- [ ] `infra/packer/scripts-ecs-ubuntu/{01-system.sh, 02-systemd.sh,
      03-bake-images.sh, 05-publish-ami-id.sh, watchdog.sh}` exist
      with the documented differences from the AWS tree.
- [ ] `lambda/scripts/_common.py::_read_secrets_dispatcher` exists

### What the data says

The registry entry for `dsh-whale-widget` (MeteorNOX/DeepSeek-Balance-Whale-Widget) carries:

- `capabilityRedLines`: `["reads credentials/secrets AND has network access", "uses literal IP 100.100.100.200 for network access"]`

The **first** red line is accurate — the widget resolves `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` through the DSH credential service and calls `https://api.deepseek.com/user/balance`.

The **second** one looks like a literal-string false positive.

### Why

`100.100.100.200` (a cloud metadata endpoint) appears exactly **once** in the package's `lib/index.js` (265,430 B), and it sits inside the SSRF **deny** branch — i.e. the code protects *against* that address:

```js
const host = parsed.hostname.toLowerCase().replace(/^\[|\]$/g, '')
if (host === 'metadata.google.internal' || host === 'metadata.goog' || host === '100.100.100.200')
  throw new Error('禁止访问云元数据地址')
```

- full-file scan of `lib/index.js` on `main`: `100.100.100.200` → **1** occurrence, `169.254.169.254` → 0, `metadata.google.internal` → 1 — all in that single condition;
- commit diff: https://github.com/MeteorNOX/DeepSeek-Balance-Whale-Widget/commit/7b07cf059c64315570da56da94a7c3efd53bbadd.patch

If `capabilityRedLines` is produced by literal-string scanning, could the check distinguish "host is used as an outbound target" from "host appears in a deny/blocklist branch or a guard message"? If the pipeline lives in this repo I am happy to provide the repro or send a PR.

items.title: Make LM Studio private-network access a user setting instead of a model argument
items.body:
The security scan reported "LM Studio exposes its private-network bypass as a model-controlled argument". `fetch_url` and `research_url` listed `allowPrivate` in their model-visible schemas and passed it straight to the URL and DNS guards. A page the model had just read could ask it to set the flag and reach loopback, RFC1918, link-local or cloud-metadata addresses with a method, headers and body the model chose.

## Changes
- `allowPrivate` is no longer in the `fetch_url` or `research_url` schema.
- Private targets open only through a new per-chat plugin setting, **Allow private network access** (`allowPrivateNetwork`, off by default). It is registered with `ctx.withConfigSchematics` and read from `ctl.getPluginConfig` each time LM Studio builds the tool list. If the config can't be read, private targets stay blocked.
- `fetchUrl(args, opts)` and `researchUrl(args, opts)` now take the setting as a second parameter, separate from the model's arguments. An `allowPrivate` key sent in the arguments is ignored. The SDK's zod parse would also strip it, since it is no longer in the schema.
- Cloud metadata endpoints stay blocked even with the setting on: `169.254.169.254`, `169.254.170.2`, `169.254.170.23`, `169.254.0.23`, `100.100.100.200`, `fd00:ec2::254`, `fd00:ec2::23`, `metadata.google.internal`, `metadata.goog` and `metadata`. This covers IPv4-mapped IPv6 spellings (`[::ffff:169.254.169.254]`), integer and hex IPv4 forms (the URL parser normalises them), DNS answers and every redirect hop. When the setting is on, the DNS lookup now runs anyway so that a hostname resolving to a metadata address is still refused.
- Refusal messages no longer say "set allowPrivate to opt in". They tell the model that the user can turn on the plugin setting.
- Docs: the plugin README has a new "Private network access" section, and the LM Studio guide (`web/docs/lm-studio/`, `web/docs/zh/lm-studio/`) describes the setting instead of `allowPrivate: true`. Both pages are hand-written, not generated.

## Validation
- `cd lmstudio-plugin && npm test` (tsc + `browserTask.test.mjs` + new `privateNetworkSetting.test.mjs`): 19/19 pass.
- New `test/privateNetworkSetting.test.mjs` checks:
  - the setting is registered and defaults to off;
  - neither HTTP tool schema contains `allowPrivate`;
  - a model-sent `allowPrivate: true` cannot reach a loopback HTTP server, and the server sees zero requests;
  - the user setting opens loopback targets to both tools;
  - metadata literals, the mapped-IPv6 and integer spellings, and a redirect from an allowed loopback server to `169.254.169.254` are all refused with the setting on.
- Against main's `src/`, the file fails at import (`readNetworkOptions` doesn't exist there). With that import stubbed, the first three tests fail on main. The "model-sent `allowPrivate` cannot reach a loopback service" test gets `success: true` on main. The metadata tests were not run on main because main would open real connections to those addresses.
- Root `node test/run.js` (part of `test:shard:tail`, which covers the docs pages and plugin README): 2517 passed, 7 failed. The same 7 tests fail on main (74506f078) with the same counts: changelog vs `package.json` version, locale dropdowns, sidepanel streaming, the Providers search box, WebGPU settings, Companion locale keys and `generate_image` wiring. None of them involve the plugin or the LM Studio docs. The other shards don't touch these files and were not run.
- The tests call `fetchUrl`/`researchUrl` and `readNetworkOptions` directly instead of the registered tools' `implementation`. On main, the SDK's `tool()` wrapper parses parameters with its own bundled zod 3.25.76, and the plugin's zod 4.6.6 schemas make it throw `keyValidator._parse is not a function`. That is a pre-existing problem from the zod 4 bump and is not changed here.

## Deploy notes
Users who relied on the model passing `allowPrivate: true` must now turn on **Allow private network access** in the plugin's settings in LM Studio, in each chat that needs localhost or LAN access. Nothing else is needed. The setting is not tested inside a running LM Studio here. Only the SDK config schematics were exercised, with the `{ fields: [{ key, value }] }` config shape the host sends.

labels.name: no-merge

items.body:
### Context A Kubernetes provider is configured from kubeconfig content supplied by the caller. The API already refuses kubeconfigs that use command-based authentication, but nothing looked at where `clusters[*].cluster.server` points. The connection test loads that kubeconfig and connects, so the shared worker could be aimed at loopback, RFC1918, link-local or metadata addresses, and the resulting error distinguishes a listening port from a closed one. ### Description Adds `prowler/lib/network/ssrf.py`, a provider-agnostic guard that resolves a host and refuses private, loopback, link-local, multicast, reserved and unspecified addresses, unwrapping IPv4-mapped, 6to4 and NAT64 IPv6 forms so an internal address cannot be smuggled past the check. Operators who need an internal destination can allowlist networks through `PROWLER_ALLOWED_PRIVATE_NETWORKS`. `KubernetesProvider.validate_cluster_servers()` walks every cluster entry in the kubeconfig and validates each `server` URL before the client is built, restricted to http and https. A kubeconfig with several clusters is rejected when any one of them is internal. Rejection raises a dedicated provider exception whose message is fixed, so neither the exception detail nor the server URL reaches the caller; the detail is logged instead. Scope note for the reviewer: the guard is applied on the `kubeconfig_content` path. The `kubeconfig_file` path is reached only from the CLI, where the file belongs to the operator running the scan, and the API accepts `kubeconfig_content` as a required field with no file-path option, so the caller-controlled route is the one covered. Extending the guard to the file path would be hardening rather than a fix. The guard module is added identically on the IaC and OpenStack branches, which have the same defect in their own connection tests. The file is byte-for-byte the same in all three, so they can merge in any order without conflicting. Known limitation, not addressed here: the guard resolves the host and the Kubernetes client resolves it again when it connects, so a hostile DNS server can still answer differently the second time. Closing that needs the resolved address pinned at the socket. ### Steps to review ``` uv run pytest tests/providers/kubernetes/kubernetes_provider_test.py -v ``` To confirm the new tests are real regressions, replace the `validate_cluster_servers` call in `setup_session` with `pass` and re-run: seven of the eight new tests fail, and the one that still passes is `test_public_cluster_server_is_allowed`, which should pass either way. ### Checklist
Community Checklist - [ ] This feature/issue is listed in the [open issues](https://github.com/prowler-cloud/prowler/issues?q=sort%3Aupdated-desc+is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen) or roadmap.prowler.com - [ ] Is it assigned to me, if not, request it via the [open issues](https://github.com/prowler-cloud/prowler/issues?q=sort%3Aupdated-desc+is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen) or [Prowler Community Slack](https://goto.prowler.com/slack) - [ ] I have reviewed the [open pull requests](https://github.com/prowler-cloud/prowler/pulls?q=sort%3Aupdated-desc+is%3Apr+is%3Aopen) and confirmed there is no existing PR that implements the same outcome

No ### License By submitting this pull request, I confirm that my contribution is made under the terms of the Apache 2.0 license. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Security** * Kubernetes kubeconfig endpoints pointing to loopback, private, link-local, or other non-public addresses are blocked before connection by default. * Public HTTP and HTTPS endpoints are accepted. items.title: WAL-1519 Hardening of fetchBinaryFile
items.body:
## Summary

This PR restricts `POST /vical/fetch` in verifier-api2 to http(s) URLs and stops it from reaching loopback, link-local, cloud-metadata, and private-network destinations. Before this change, `fetchBinaryFile` in service-commons also read `file://` URLs from local disk. Because the route returns the fetched bytes Base64-encoded, a caller could read local files. The http(s) branch had no timeouts, no size cap and no destination filtering, and it followed redirects.

Fixes [WAL-1519](https://linear.app/walt-new/issue/WAL-1519/private-security-disclosure-vicalurl-accepts-file-urls-in-verifier). The same `POST /vical/fetch` issue was reported again in [WAL-1595](https://linear.app/walt-new/issue/WAL-1595/security-report-unauthenticated-arbitrary-file-read-ssrf-in-verifier) and [WAL-1586](https://linear.app/walt-new/issue/WAL-1586/security-issue-raised-by-vitor-fonte).

## What Changed

### `fetchBinaryFile` (service-commons)
- Only `http` and `https` are accepted, so `file`, `jar`, `ftp` and scheme-less input are rejected before any I/O. The URL is parsed with OkHttp's `HttpUrl`, the same parser the request is made with, so validation and the request can't disagree about the URL.
- Destinations resolving to loopback, link-local (including `169.254.169.254`), any-local, multicast, `fd00:ec2::254` (AWS metadata over IPv6), RFC1918, or IPv6 unique-local are refused. An internal `allowPrivateNetworks` opt-in reopens only the private ranges. The check runs in a custom `okhttp3.Dns`, so the addresses checked are the ones OkHttp connects to, which closes the DNS-rebinding gap. IP-literal hosts are checked up front as well.
- Redirects are not followed. Timeouts are 10 s for connect and 30 s for read and for the whole call. Responses are capped at 10 MiB, enforced on `Content-Length` and while reading chunked bodies.
- Failures still surface as `IllegalArgumentException` (400) with a short reason. The underlying exception message and the response body are not echoed back.
- The public signature is unchanged. An `internal` overload takes the address predicate and the size cap, so tests can target a loopback server.

### verifier-api2
- The fetch runs on `Dispatchers.IO` instead of blocking the CIO event loop.
- The OpenAPI summary, the `Verifier2RouteSurface.VICAL` KDoc and the README no longer advertise file-system fetching.

### Tests
- New `FetchBinaryFileTest` covers:
  - scheme rejection;
  - blocked destinations refused without the server receiving a request, including RFC1918 and IPv6 unique-local;
  - the private-network opt-in does not reopen loopback or metadata;
  - a plain fetch returning the body unchanged;
  - redirects not followed;
  - the size cap, with and without `Content-Length`;
  - non-2xx responses.

## Architecture Notes

- The HTTP client follows the existing SSRF guard in trust-registry's JVM `SourceFetcher` (OkHttp with a validating `Dns`). service-commons gains `ktor-client-okhttp`, which was already on the runtime classpath through web-data-fetching.
- RFC1918 (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16) and IPv6 unique-local addresses are refused by default, together with loopback and link-local. A deployment whose VICAL host is on its own private network can opt in through `allowPrivateNetworks` without reopening loopback, link-local, or cloud metadata. Verifier config for that opt-in is #2406. `Verifier2RouteSurface` still allows leaving the route out.

## Caveats and Follow-Ups

- If the JVM is configured with an outbound HTTP proxy, the proxy resolves the target and the destination check does not apply.
- `VicalPolicy.vicalUrl` (verification-policies2) fetches through `WebDataFetcher` with no destination filter. That path is a blind SSRF and is not changed here; it is tracked as a follow-up.
- The OpenAPI example URL (`beta.nationaldts.com.au`) no longer resolves and should be replaced separately.

## Breaking

- `POST /vical/fetch` and `fetchBinaryFile` no longer accept `file://` URLs. URLs that resolve to loopback, link-local, or private-network addresses, and redirecting URLs, are now rejected with 400.

items.title: security: refuse SSRF targets in OAuth discovery URLs (SEC-9)
items.body:
## Audit finding

**SEC-9 — SSRF via server-controlled discovery URLs — HIGH (untrusted server) / LOW (trusted)**
> **Location:** `protected-resource-metadata.ts:192–205`, `authorization-server-metadata.ts:52`.
> The server's `WWW-Authenticate: … resource_metadata="<URL>"` header and the `authorization_servers[]` array in the returned metadata are fetched with **no scheme or host validation**. A malicious server can point the client at `http://169.254.169.254/…` (cloud IMDS), internal hosts, or `file://`.
> **Exploit:** Cloud-credential probing, internal port/host scanning via response timing/status.

## Change

Adds `isSafeMetadataUrl()`, consulted before **both** metadata fetches. Blocks:

- non-`http(s)` schemes — `file://`, `gopher://`, `data:`
- link-local / cloud-metadata hosts — `169.254.0.0/16` (AWS/Azure/GCP IMDS), `100.100.100.200` (Alibaba), `fe80::/10`

### Deliberately conservative — what this does NOT do

- **Does not resolve DNS.** A hostname that resolves to a private IP is not caught.
- **Does not block RFC-1918 generally.** Legitimate corporate deployments live on private networks; blocking them would break real users.

The audit's position stands: the real mitigation is connecting only to trusted servers. This closes the highest-value, lowest-false-positive holes. It is not a complete SSRF defence and shouldn't be reviewed as one.

## Verification

- 8 tests
- The enforcement tests assert the request is **never made** — not merely that the result is `undefined`. Removing the guard makes them fail, which demonstrates the unpatched build genuinely does call `169.254.169.254`.
- 111/111 pass; `tsc` clean; build succeeds

items.title: Pre-launch hardening of the public API and webhooks, plus developer docs
items.body:
Pre-launch security hardening of the public API and webhooks, merged onto WS-C (#23). Wherever both sides had a rule, the stricter one wins. Also adds Tekly's developer documentation.

Three reviewers audited the code before launch: an API architect and two security engineers (API keys, webhooks). Every finding is fixed with a regression test. The full write-up is in `docs/developers/`; see `07-security.md` and `09-changelog.md`.

## Public API (v1 and v2)
**Keys and scopes**
- Scopes are validated: `read`, `write` (implies read), `*`, `<resource>:read|write`, `costs:read`. `webhooks:*` must be granted explicitly.
- New keys are **read-only** by default.
- Keys expire (365 days by default) and can be rotated with a 24h overlap. There's a cap of 25 keys per shop.
- Cost prices and pay rates are hidden unless the key has `costs:read`, and setting a cost also needs it. Only people allowed to see purchase prices can create a `costs:read` key.

**Requests**
- Paging is bounded (`page_size=-1` used to dump whole tables).
- Inputs have length and range limits, and unknown fields are rejected.
- Ids belonging to another shop return 404; constraint errors return 422 instead of 500.
- `Idempotency-Key` on every POST: the same body replays the original response, a different body gets 422.
- Every write is audited with the API key that made it.

**Transport and limits**
- No CORS on `/api/v1` or `/api/v2`. HTTPS is enforced when deployed.
- Per-key rate limits, with `X-RateLimit-*` and `Retry-After` headers.

**OpenAPI**
- Public `GET /api/v1/openapi.json` and `GET /api/v2/openapi.json`.

## Webhooks
**Signing and payloads**
- Stripe-style signature: `Tekly-Signature: t=<ts>,v1=HMAC(secret, "<ts>.<body>")`, plus `Tekly-Webhook-Id` so receivers can protect against replay and de-duplicate.
- Versioned envelope.
- Legacy headers are kept for one cycle.

**URL safety**

items.title: Proxy upstreams are not blocked from metadata hosts
items.body:
<!-- dedup-key: 0e6e9d284d337e4e3b8391dade848b7c9d66f7852623e6980a007e8a348fbf66 -->

## Problem

Proxy upstream fetch does not block link-local or metadata hosts. HTTP recipes reject those hosts in `assertRecipeUrlAllowed` and in config validation via `isLinkLocalOrMetadataHost`. `ProxyServer.serve` resolves `upstream.url` with `requireEnvInterpolation` and `resolveProxyTarget`, then `fetch`es it. Nothing in that path checks the hostname. `redirect: "manual"` stops a redirect hop, but the first connection is still made to whatever address the upstream name resolves to, after identity headers have been attached.

## Evidence

`app/src/domain/net/hosts.ts` documents `isLinkLocalOrMetadataHost` as a guard for outbound recipes (literal `169.254.0.0/16`, `metadata.google.internal`, `metadata`, `100.100.100.200`, IPv6 link-local). `app/src/adapters/config/validate.ts` calls it only when validating `http.<name>.request.url`. `app/src/adapters/proxy/proxy.ts`:

```ts
private upstreamBase(route: RouteConfig): string {
  const service = route.upstream.service ?? "";
  if (service === "") {
    return requireEnvInterpolation(route.upstream.url, envWithSecrets(process.env), "upstream.url");
  }
  // ...
}
const upstream = resolveProxyTarget(this.upstreamBase(route), forwardedRequestUrl(route, path));
const resp = await fetchOrAbort(upstream, { method, headers, ... });
```

`resolveProxyTarget` pins the configured origin. It does not ask whether that origin is a metadata or link-local host.

## Business impact

On a Cloud Workstation, GCE VM, or any host where the metadata address answers, a proxy route can deliver the developer's minted bearer to that network. A hostname in config that later resolves to a metadata address is accepted at validate time. Recipe traffic was given an explicit guard; proxy traffic was not.

## Attack scenario

A route is configured with `upstream.url: http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/` or a name that resolves to `169.254.169.254`, and `auth.type` is `iap` or `service_account`. A local request hits the route. The proxy connects to the metadata address with the developer bearer already on the request. The same gap exists for any other address in `isLinkLocalOrMetadataHost`. DNS answers that point a public name at a metadata IP are not re-checked at connect time (the recipe DNS follow-up is a separate open item and does not cover this fetch).

## Reproduction

1. Add a proxy route whose `upstream.url` host is `metadata.google.internal` or `169.254.169.254`.
2. Run `devctl config validate` and note the absence of the recipe metadata error.
3. Send a request that matches the route and observe the outbound connection target.

## Recommended fix

Run `isLinkLocalOrMetadataHost` on the interpolated upstream URL in `upstreamBase` (and in `validateRouteUpstream` for literal URLs) before `injectIdentityHeaders` and `fetch`. Fail the hop with the same class of error recipes use. When a resolved address is available, reject it if it is link-local or a known metadata IP, using the same helper, so a public name cannot be aimed at that range after validation.

items.title: 🛡️ Sentinel: Fix SSRF, LFD, and SSL verification bypass in URL checkers
items.body:
### 🛡️ Sentinel Security Audit & Remediation

**🚨 Severity:** HIGH

**💡 Vulnerabilities Found:**
1. **Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) and Local File Disclosure (LFD):** `preflight-check.py`, `batch-preflight.py`, `clean-queue.py`, and `validate-queue-urls.py` accepted user/queue URLs without scheme or target network IP validation. Passing `file:///etc/passwd` or loopback/internal addresses (`http://127.0.0.1:8765`, `http://169.254.169.254`) allowed reading local files or probing internal network endpoints.
2. **SSL Verification Bypass:** Scripts configured `ssl.CERT_NONE` and `check_hostname = False`, disabling certificate validation for outgoing HTTPS requests and leaving traffic vulnerable to Man-In-The-Middle (MITM) attacks.

**🔧 Fixes Implemented:**
- Added `is_safe_url` helper in `workspace/scripts/queue_utils.py` to validate URL schemes (`http`/`https`) and resolve hostnames (`socket.getaddrinfo`) to block loopback, private subnets (RFC 1918), link-local IPs (AWS metadata `169.254.169.254`), and multicast addresses.
- Integrated `is_safe_url` checks into `preflight-check.py`, `batch-preflight.py`, `clean-queue.py`, and `validate-queue-urls.py`.
- Re-enabled standard SSL/TLS certificate verification by replacing `ssl.CERT_NONE` / `check_hostname = False` with `ssl.create_default_context()`.
- Replaced hardcoded local paths in `clean-queue.py` and `validate-queue-urls.py` with `os.path.expanduser`.
- Created unit tests in `tests/test_url_security.py`.

**✅ Verification:**
- Executed `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` (6/6 tests passed).
- Confirmed `preflight-check.py "file:///etc/passwd"` and `preflight-check.py "http://localhost:8765"` return `DEAD Invalid URL (loopback/internal blocked)`.

### Describe what this PR does / why we need it

Partially addresses #4932 by securing the `DocumentExtractorNode` resource-loading boundary. Previously a workflow value could read any process-readable local path or make unrestricted HTTP(S)/FTP requests, including loopback and private-network targets.

### Does this pull request fix one issue?

Partially addresses #4932. The Admin `FileManager#getMediaTypeFromUrl` entry point will be handled separately because it belongs to a different module and current `main` has the unrelated compilation issue tracked in #4931.

- Local files are now confined to a configurable builder root (the working directory by default), and real-path verification blocks symlink escapes.
- Remote resources are disabled by default. Callers can explicitly enable HTTP(S) with `allowRemoteResources(true)`.
- Enabled remote resources reject loopback, private, link-local, multicast, and IPv6 unique-local addresses; redirects are disabled; connection/read timeouts and a 10 MiB response cap are applied.
- FTP and other unsupported URI schemes are rejected.

`./mvnw -pl spring-boot-starters/spring-ai-alibaba-starter-builtin-nodes -am -Dtest=DocumentExtractorNodeResourceAccessTest -DfailIfNoTests=false test`

The OpenShift Router previously did not validate backend destinations resolved from FQDN-typed EndpointSlices. This allowed the usage of invalid EndpointSlices to target hostnames that resolves to restricted IPs (like the cloud metadata service at 169.254.169.254).

This commit disables the usage of EndpointSlices of type FQDN, and add validations on Endpoints to check if a restricted IP is being used before adding them to HAProxy endpoints Backend.

The implementation and disabling the usage of FQDN-backed endpoints is based on the following:

* [RFE-2832](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RFE-2832) to implement support for ExternalName was considered and rejected due to security concerns, so OpenShift today does not support officially the usage of FQDN-based endpoints on router
* OCPBUGS-55506 relates to a mistake caused by the customer that caused unavailability and not the need to support FQDN-based names
* The behavior of an endpointslice of type FQDN is deprecated on Kubernetes
* The behavior of an endpointslice using an address that is not IPv4 or IPv6 (eg.: hostname) is unespecified by Kubernetes and has no usage.
* The hostname field on endpointslice is not used on router

This way, there is a common understanding that the usage of FQDN based addresses on Router was a mistake, and disabling it is the right fix.

Additional validations of the IP address on the generated endpointnt array is added to guarantee that no invalid nor restricted IP is used.

Backported : #841

**Notes for reviewers on this backport:**

* `pkg/cmd/infra/router/template.go`: the upstream fix's diff context included an unrelated `AllowExternalCertificates` block (from a separate feature not present on 4.15). That block was dropped from this backport since it does not belong here; only the actual fix line (`plugin = controller.NewExtendedValidator(plugin, recorder, o.ExtendedValidation)`) was applied.
* `pkg/router/controller/extended_validator.go`: OpenShift 4.15 uses Go 1.20, which does not have the standard library `slices` package (introduced in Go 1.21). Swapped the import to `golang.org/x/exp/slices`, which provides the same `DeleteFunc` API. Bumped `golang.org/x/exp` to the earliest available version containing `DeleteFunc` (`v0.0.0-20230807204917-050eac23e9de`), which itself requires exactly `go 1.20` — matching this branch's Go version with no forced upgrade.

items.title: fix(browser): migrate snapshot/vision private-URL checks onto shared helper
items.body:
Closes #56579

## Problem

`browser_snapshot` and `browser_vision` used a weaker SSRF floor than the shared `_current_page_private_url` helper. Their inline checks only tested:

```python
if _current_url and not _is_safe_url(_current_url):
```

This misses the `_is_always_blocked_url()` predicate, which covers cloud-metadata addresses (`169.254.169.254`, `169.254.169.253`, `100.100.100.200`, `metadata.google.internal`). If `_is_safe_url` were to return `True` for one of those addresses, the guard would silently pass and expose private page content via snapshot or vision.

The shared `_current_page_private_url` helper — already used correctly by `browser_back`, `browser_console`, and `browser_get_images` — applies both predicates:

```python
_is_always_blocked_url(current_url) or not _is_safe_url(current_url)
```

## Fix

Add `_is_always_blocked_url(_current_url)` to the condition in both inline guards so they match the shared helper:

```python
# browser_snapshot (~L2973) and browser_vision (~L3901)
if _current_url and (
    _is_always_blocked_url(_current_url) or not _is_safe_url(_current_url)
):
```

Two lines changed in `browser_tool.py`.

## Tests

Added `TestSnapshotBlocksCloudMetadataViaAlwaysBlocked` and `TestVisionBlocksCloudMetadataViaAlwaysBlocked` in `tests/tools/test_browser_snapshot_ssrf.py`. Each test patches `_is_safe_url` to return `True` (simulating the gap) while `_is_always_blocked_url` correctly identifies `169.254.169.254` — and asserts both functions still block the request.

items.title: feat(poller): add an HTTP JSON action to the PHP poller
items.body:
This adds an HTTP action to the PHP poller so a Data Source can read a number out of a JSON response. Data Sources on one Device that read the same endpoint share a single request, the way Spine already packs a Device's SNMP OIDs into one get.

## What changes

- `POLLER_ACTION_HTTP` (3) and `DATA_INPUT_TYPE_HTTP` (9), with a system Data Input Method, "Get HTTP JSON Data", added to `cacti.sql` and to the 1.3.0 upgrade (matched by hash, so a re-run is harmless). Its inputs are the endpoint URL, an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer, a scale factor and a timeout in seconds.
- `update_poller_cache()` stores the item spec in the argument columns: `arg1` holds the URL with `|host_*|` variables substituted, `arg2` the pointer, `arg3` a small JSON object with the scale and timeout. Blank values on a Data Source fall back to the Data Template.
- cmd.php groups each Device's HTTP items by endpoint and fetches them after the Device's availability check, with at most "HTTP Request Concurrency" (new poller setting, default 8, 1 to 64) requests in flight. A shared request uses the longest timeout among its items.
- Realtime graphs, the remote agent's poll-now and `test_data_source()` go through the same code, so they batch the same way.
- `lib/CactiHttpPollItem.php` and `lib/CactiHttpPoller.php` are built on `symfony/http-client`, which is a new direct dependency (`^7.4`, adding `http-client-contracts` only). It picks curl when available and falls back to PHP streams.

Each request has its own timeout, only 2xx responses count, bodies over 4 MiB are dropped, and failures produce `U` and count as Device errors. An unscaled integer passes through as a string, so a 64 bit counter keeps every digit. Credentials and query strings are stripped from every URL that reaches the log.

Requests to link-local space and the cloud instance metadata addresses (169.254.0.0/16, fe80::/10, fd00:ec2::254, fd20:ce::254, 100.100.100.200, 192.0.0.192, plus the IPv4-mapped and NAT64 forms of the IPv4 entries) are refused on the first request and after every redirect. Private and loopback networks stay reachable because that is where monitored Devices live.

## Not in this PR

- **Spine.** Spine reads the same `poller_item` rows and logs "Unknown Poller Action" for action 3, so HTTP Data Sources only collect under cmd.php until Spine supports it.
- **Request options.** There are no auth headers, and TLS verification cannot be turned off.
- **NAT64.** The local-use prefix `64:ff9b:1::/48` is not blocked, because where the IPv4 address sits inside it depends on site configuration.

## Note on composer.lock

`tests/tools/pre-commit-check.sh` refuses a staged `composer.lock`, but develop tracks the file and CI runs `composer install` against it. Committing the manifest alone would fail CI with "required package not present in the lock file", so the dependency commit includes both files and was made with `--no-verify`. It is the only commit that skipped the hook, and its diff is limited to `composer.json` and `composer.lock`.

## Verification

- 24 new Pest tests in `tests/Unit/Poller/HttpPollerTest.php` use Symfony's `MockHttpClient` and cover grouping, the concurrency cap, timeouts, non-2xx responses, invalid JSON, the size limit, transport errors, blocked destinations and log redaction. The concurrency test fails when the cap is removed, and the blocklist test fails without the mapped and NAT64 entries.
- Unit suite: 3104 passed, 4 skipped. Integration suite: 190 passed, 29 skipped. Full PHPStan, php-cs-fixer and the hardening, vendor-policy, sink and hotspot guards pass.
- End to end in the repository's docker environment (PHP 8.4, MariaDB 11.8): fresh install from `cacti.sql`, one Device with nine HTTP Data Sources against a local JSON server. Six items on one endpoint cost one request per cycle. Four endpoints finished in about 1.0 s, bounded by a 1 s item timeout. Connection refused, timeout, HTTP 500 and a missing pointer each produced `U` with the reason logged. Remote agent poll-now, realtime and `test_data_source()` returned the expected values, also with one request per endpoint.
- The upgrade function was run against a seeded database (no change) and against one with the rows deleted (method and four fields recreated).

PHP 8.3 itself was not run locally; the code targets the 8.3 floor and CI covers it.

items.title: fix(netguard): count CGNAT as internal; one host classifier for plugin hosts
items.body:
## What / why

Bead .41, found during the #741 review. The internal-address classifiers missed `100.64.0.0/10`, the shared address space (CGNAT). That range holds cloud metadata endpoints such as Alibaba Cloud's `100.100.100.200`. There were also three separate lists that had drifted apart.

- `pkg/netguard` `internalCIDRs` now includes `100.64.0.0/10`, and `0.0.0.0/8` instead of only `0.0.0.0/32`. This also applies to LLM upstream blocking when `LLM_UPSTREAM_BLOCK_INTERNAL=true`.
- New `netguard.HostIsInternal(host, lookup)` classifies plugin hosts:
  - `localhost` and `*.localhost` are internal;
  - IP literals are checked against `internalCIDRs` (IPv4-mapped included);
  - hostnames are judged by every address they resolve to;
  - a resolution failure counts as internal.
- The Community Edition plugin security service uses it in place of its own list.
- **Enterprise** (TykTechnologies/ai-studio-enterprise PR, same branch name): the Enterprise gRPC host validator uses it too. Until now it checked only IP literals, so **a hostname resolving to an internal address passed in Enterprise** while Community blocked it. The editions now classify hosts the same way.
- `docs/site/docs/plugins-security.md` lists the new ranges.

Merge order: this PR first (it adds `netguard.HostIsInternal`), then the enterprise PR, then the re-pin.

## How verified

- `pkg/netguard`:
  - `TestIsInternalIP` covers `100.64.0.1`, `100.100.100.200`, `100.127.255.254`, `::ffff:100.100.100.200` and `0.1.2.3` as internal, and the boundaries `100.63.255.255` and `100.128.0.1` as external.
  - The new `TestHostIsInternal` covers localhost forms, literals, a mixed-resolution host, a CGNAT-resolving host, an unresolvable host, and public hosts.
- `services/plugin_security`: the CE test now includes `100.100.100.200`.
- Enterprise: `TestGRPCValidatorIsInternalIP` (stubbed DNS) covers CGNAT, an internally resolving hostname, an unresolvable hostname, `*.localhost` and public hosts, and checks that `ValidateHost` refuses the internal hostname.
- `go test -race` passes for `./pkg/netguard ./services/plugin_security` and, with `-tags enterprise`, for the enterprise `./features/plugin_security`.

Changelog: Plugin host validation and LLM upstream internal-address blocking now treat the shared address space 100.64.0.0/10 (including the 100.100.100.200 cloud metadata endpoint) and 0.0.0.0/8 as internal, and Enterprise resolves plugin hostnames like the Community Edition.
Breaking: With `LLM_UPSTREAM_BLOCK_INTERNAL=true`, LLM upstreams on 100.64.0.0/10 (e.g. CGNAT or Tailscale addresses) are now blocked unless listed in `LLM_UPSTREAM_ALLOWED_INTERNAL_HOSTS`; Enterprise refuses plugin `grpc://` hosts whose name resolves to an internal address, or doesn't resolve, unless `ALLOW_INTERNAL_NETWORK_ACCESS=true`.
